headline: Portland City Council to vote on affordable housing funding, data center rules, and winter warming shelter funds.
summary: The council will consider liquor license approvals, affordable housing financing for Boyd and Cumberland Housing and Lambert Woods North, data center regulations, and funding for a winter warming shelter and public health grants. It will also discuss Council rules, a Forest Avenue pedestrian project, parking fee changes, and testimony on a Central Maine Power transmission project.

RESOLUTIONS: 
  
 Resolve 4-26/27 Requesting Ordinance Amendments Regulating Data Centers in the 
City of Portland - Sponsored by Housing & Economic Development Committee, 
Councilor Pious Ali, Chair 
    
  
At its meeting on October 6, 2026, the Housing and Economic Development Committee 
reviewed and voted to the send this Resolution for Council consideration. The Resolution 
requests that the Director of Planning and Urban Development initiate the process for 
amendments to the City’s Land Use Code and develop amendments for consideration by
3 
the Planning Board and City Council that address the development of Data Centers 
within the City of Portland. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Resolve 5-26/27 Authorizing The Mayor to Submit Testimony to the Public Utilities 
Commission To Protect The Public's Right to Provide Comment On Central Maine 
Power's Request for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for the 
Construction of Transmission Upgrades in Portland and the Greater Portland Area 
- Sponsored by Mark Dion, Mayor 
    
  
Central Maine Power has submitted to the Public Utilities Commission a request for a 
Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for the construction of certain 
transmission upgrades in Portland and the Greater Portland area.  City Councilors and 
local residents have raised concerns regarding the public's receipt of notice and 
opportunity to be heard by CMP and the PUC in connection with the project and the 
project's environmental and other impacts on public and private property. This resolution 
would authorize the Mayor to submit testimony on behalf of the City to the PUC as 
needed to protect the rights of the City's residents to provide comment on the project.  
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
UNFINISHED BUSINESS: 
  
 Resolve 3-26/27 Amending Council Rules - Sponsored by Rules Committee, 
Councilor Pious Ali, Chair 
    
  
The Rules Committee met on August 26, 2026, and voted to forward this item to the City 
Council for consideration. The proposed amendments to the City Council's Rules of 
Procedure would update Rule 13 to allow the Peaks Island Council to sponsor agenda 
items directly, and also modify Rule 29 to enable the City Council to formally refer items 
to the Peaks Island Council with specific instructions, timelines, and guidelines. 
Councilor Grant has offered an amendment that removes the Peaks Island Council's 
authority to sponsor agenda items and deletes the specific procedures required when 
referring items to it, as set forth in the Grant Amendment 1 attached hereto. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on September 21 
and its second reading on October 5, at which point it was postponed to October 19. Five 
affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Order 55-26/27 Approving an Amendment to the Boyd Housing and Cumberland 
Housing Affordable Housing Development and Tax Increment Financing District 
and Adopting the Amended Municipal Development Program for the District - 
Sponsored by Housing & Economic Development Committee, Councilor Pious Ali, 
Chair 
    
  
The Housing and Economic Development Committee voted 4-0 to move this request 
forward to City Council. On August 11, 2025, the City Council approved the Boyd and 
Cumberland Housing Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing (AHTIF) district. 
Located in Portland’s East Bayside neighborhood, this development project aims to bring 
91 units of mixed-income housing to the area, including 81 units designated as affordable 
housing. The proposed plans feature a single 7-story building complemented by shared
4 
outdoor green space for residents. Portland Housing Development Corporation is 
requesting an amendment to the existing AHTIF district for the project. 
 
To maximize available equity for a development of this scale, the project was originally 
structured as a Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) “Twin.” To support the 
original twin model, the City of Portland created one AHTIF district, called Cumberland 
and Boyd Housing, with two sets of legal documents, each named for a portion of the 
twin project (Cumberland Housing, Boyd Housing). Because the project was converted to 
a 4% LIHTC plus State LIHTC model, it is now considered one project, and the 
separation is moot. The attached documents reflect this change. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 5. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Order 56-26/27 Approving an Amended Credit Enhancement Agreement for the 
Boyd and Cumberland Housing Affordable Housing and Tax Increment Financing 
District - Sponsored by Housing & Economic Development Committee, Councilor 
Pious Ali, Chair 
    
  
On September 15, 2026 the Housing and Economic Development Committee voted (4-0) 
to recommend this item to the City Council. 
 
This is a companion order to the order above. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 5. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Order 57-26/27 Appropriating $375,000 from the Jill C. Duson Housing Trust Fund 
to Preservation of Affordable Housing RE: Lambert Woods North 622 Auburn 
Street - Sponsored by Housing & Economic Development Committee, Councilor 
Pious Ali, Chair 
    
  
At their meeting on September 15, 2026, the Housing and Economic Development 
Committee voted 4-0 to move this request to City Council for consideration. Preservation 
of Affordable Housing (POAH) has submitted a request for a loan in the amount of 
$1,328,316 from the Jill C. Duson Housing Trust Fund. Preservation of Affordable 
Housing (POAH) is requesting $1,328,316 in funding for Lambert Woods North, a 
proposed development located on city-owned land at 622 Auburn Street (future address: 
2274 Washington Avenue) and comprising 72 apartments across 6 residential buildings. 
 
The project requested $360,000 from the City of Portland’s Jill C. Duson Housing Trust 
Fund in October 2025 to address a gap caused by the loss of 45L Energy Tax Credits, 
which were eliminated by the federal government, and design changes which led to 
increased engineering, architecture, and legal costs. That request was rewarded. 
 
The project had additional design changes, requested by MaineHousing, that led to 
significant increases in costs. For a more thorough explanation of the cost increases, 
please see the attached memo from Preservation of Affordable Housing dated June 16, 
2026.  
 
Due, in part, to the additional design changes, the project closed in 2025 with a funding
5 
gap, which was filled by three bridge loans from POAH for a total of $1,559,927.  After 
an internal evaluation of the budget included in the aforementioned memo, which 
included a review and consultation with the City’s underwriter, staff recommends partial 
support of the funding request made by Lambert Woods North LLC. Staff recommends 
partial funding in the amount of $375,000 to address increases in construction hard costs, 
architect, design, survey, engineering & legal costs, as well as soft cost contingency.  
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 5. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 58-26/27 Approving Modification 3 to Pedestrian Crossing Improvements on 
Forest Avenue Project Between the Maine Department of Transportation and 
Portland - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
This project is a Locally Administered Project (LAP) where the City administers the 
projectand receives 80% funding from the state. Signing the amended partnership 
agreement enables the City to proceed with the design phase of the project and will 
continue to obligate MaineDOT to pay for 80% of the estimated project cost, or 
$160,000.00. The City will commit 20% of this estimated cost, $40,000, in matching 
funds. The original agreement between the City and MaineDOT allocated a 20% match 
of $16,000 in 2024, although with expanded scope and labor rates this fee has similarly 
increased. 
 
Modifications 1 and 2 added project scope and increased the total project amount to 
$134,532.34. Additional funding is needed to cover MaineDOT administrative costs and 
to account for the actual design costs that have been incurred. The additional funding for 
this has been allocated through the Capital Improvement Project process. This additional 
funding will result in full design completion for this project. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on October 5. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
ORDERS: 
  
 Order 63-26/27 Adopting the Civilian Police Review Board Training Procedures - 
Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
Section 2-85(a)(8) permits the Civilian Police Review Board (CPRB) to make rules 
governing their administrative procedures, subject to City Council approval. The CPRB 
approved the proposed Training Procedures at its meeting on September 23, 2026, which 
require members to complete all trainings outlined in Section 2-85(e) of the City Code as 
well as additional trainings, such as a police ride-along, and encourages ongoing training 
for Board members. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 Order 64-26/27 Accepting and Appropriating a Federal Emergency Management 
Agency Assistance to Firefighters Grant - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City 
Manager 
    
  This order authorizes the acceptance of $73,920 in Federal funding from the Fiscal Year 
2025 Assistance to Firefighters Grant Program. This funding will be used to purchase
6 
NFPA 1801 compliant thermal imaging cameras for the Fire Department. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. In order to meet the grant deadline for 
acceptance, staff is requesting that the second reading be waived, which requires seven 
affirmative votes. Staff also requests that this item be passed as an emergency. Seven 
votes are required for passage as an emergency following public comment. 
    
 Order 65-26/27 Accepting and Appropriating a Department of Health and Human 
Services Drug Free Communities Grant - Sponsored by Danielle P West, City 
Manager 
    
  
If approved, this item would accept a $625,000 ($125,000/yr for 5 years) Drug Free 
Communities grant from the U.S. CDC. Funds are meant to support the Portland 
Prevention Coalition in preventing youth substance use by strengthening local 
partnerships and addressing the community conditions that contribute to substance use. 
The goal is to build sustainable, community-driven strategies that reduce youth use of 
substances such as alcohol, tobacco, marijuana, and other drugs.  
 
This item must be read on two separate days. Due to time constraints for accepting the 
funds, staff is requesting that the second reading be waived, which requires seven 
affirmative votes. Staff also requests that this item be passed as an emergency. Seven 
votes are required for passage as an emergency following public comment. 
    
 Order 66-26/27 Traffic Schedule Amendment RE: Lancaster Street - Sponsored by 
Sustainability & Transportation Committee, Councilor Regina Phillips, Chair 
    
  
The S&T Committee met on September 16, 2026 and unanimously voted to recommend 
changes to the traffic schedule on Lancaster St. There is an existing commercial loading 
zone that is currently underutilized. The designation of parking spaces would convert to 1 
hour time zone spaces and be included in the Portland High School approved parking 
spaces.  
 
This item must be read on two separate days. This is its first reading. 
    
 Order 67-26/27 Approving the Administrative Fee Increase for Parking in the First 
Light Commons Parking Lots - Sponsored by Sustainability & Transportation 
Committee, Councilor Regina Phillips, Chair 
    
  
The S&T Committee met on September 16, 2026 and unanimously voted to recommend 
a new parking rate structure in the parking lots adjacent to First Light Commons. The 
proposed rate would align with the rate of the city operated parking garages and provide 
10 free time zone spaces that will be included in residential zone 11.  
 
This item must be read on two separate days. This is its first reading. 
    
 Order 68-26/27 Approving the Appropriation of $350,000 from the Opioid 
Settlement Fund for Operation of Emergency Winter Warming Shelter - Sponsored 
by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
If passed, this Order would allocate $350,000 from the Opioid Settlement Fund to operate 
a 2026-2027 Winter Warming Shelter in Portland. This funding would be intended to 
supplement emergency winter warming shelter funding provided by the Maine State 
Housing Authority.
7 
 
Details regarding warming shelter operations, including location, will be finalized and 
published before the Council's consideration of this item on November 2, 2026. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. This is its first reading. 
    
EXECUTIVE SESSION: 
  
 
Pursuant 1 M.R.S. section 405(6)(A) & (E), the City Council is expected to enter 
executive session to (1) discuss compensation for the Corporation Counsel, and (2) 
consult with its attorneys concerning the Council's legal rights and duties in 
connection with the Central Maine Power transmission upgrade project currently 
pending before the Public Utilities Commission.
